{{Short description|American chemist (born 1952}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=November 2021}}
'''Richard D. DiMarchi''' (born December 5, 1952<ref name=nihf>{{Cite web |url=https://www.invent.org/inductees/richard-dimarchi |title=Richard DiMarchi |access-date=January 26, 2024 |publisher=National Inventors Hall of Fame}}</ref>) is an American pharmaceutical chemist, academic, and businessman. He is the current [[chairman]] in [[Biomolecular|biomolecular sciences]] and [[professor]] of [[chemistry]] at [[Indiana University Bloomington|Indiana University]]. He is most notable for his work as a former [[vice president]] at [[Eli Lilly and Company]].

He received his [[bachelor's degree]] from [[Florida Atlantic University]] in 1974, and his [[doctorate]] from [[Indiana University]] in 1979.<ref>{{cite web | title = Department of Chemistry at Indiana University – Richard D. DiMarchi | publisher = Indiana University Department of Chemistry | url=http://dimarchi.chem.indiana.edu/ | accessdate = November 24, 2006}}</ref> He did his [[postdoctoral research]] at [[Rockefeller University]] under the mentorship of [[Nobel laureate]] [[Robert Bruce Merrifield]].<ref name=cen>{{Cite web |last=McCoy |first=Michael |date=October 5, 2015 |title=C&EN Talks With Richard DiMarchi |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/93/i39/CEN-Talks-Richard-DiMarchi.html |work=Chemical & Engineering News}}</ref>

DiMarchi recently developed a synthetic analog of the human version of the hormone [[glucagon]]. DiMarchi's glucagon analog possesses similar biological properties to natural glucagon. It dissolves easily and maintains its structural integrity over extended periods at room temperature.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://newsinfo.iu.edu/web/page/normal/3929.html|title=Richard DiMarchi is CICP's Innovator of the Year|publisher=Indiana University|accessdate=December 1, 2009}}</ref>

DiMarchi left Eli Lilly in 2003 after working for 22 years, and has since founded six biotech companies based on the research he began there.<ref name=bb>{{Cite news |last=Muller |first=Madison |date=January 26, 2024 |title=How a Lucky Break Fueled Eli Lilly's $600 Billion Weight-Loss Empire |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2024-01-26/zepbound-how-eli-lilly-s-lucky-break-fueled-a-600b-weight-loss-empire |work=Bloomberg Businessweek}}</ref> He co-founded Ambrx along with [[Peter G. Schultz]], that modifies therapeutic proteins to  treat metabolic-related diseases, and later acquired by a Chinese consortium in 2015. In 2006, his lab at Indiana University spun off Marcadia Biotech, focusing on obesity and diabetes. It was sold to [[Roche]] in 2010, where DiMarchi worked on a part-time basis for three years. He co-founded Calibrium and MB2 in 2013 and 2015, respectively, both of which were eventually acquired by [[Novo (company)|Novo]].<ref name=cen /><ref name=bb />

He is the Linda & Jack Gill Chair in Biomolecular Sciences and Professor of Chemistry at Indiana University. He was inducted into the [[National Inventors Hall of Fame]] in 2014 for his role in the scientific advancements that led to the development of some of the first [[Recombinant DNA|rDNA]]-derived medicines, including [[Humalog]] and [[Forteo]].<ref name=nihf /> The following year, he was elected as member of the [[National Academy of Medicine]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.insideindianabusiness.com/articles/dimarchi-adds-another-honor |title=DiMarchi Adds Another Honor |date=October 21, 2015 |website=Inside Indiana Business}}</ref> In 2016, he received the Alfred Burger Award in Medicinal Chemistry from [[American Chemical Society]].<ref name=cen />
